_about: HearthDAoC's additions to upstream's classic-quests.json; ClassicQuests reads both. The Guild of Shadows level-50 "Lord of Deceit" quests (one per class, added by deploy/bin/epic_chains.py): stage 1 kill Lord Elidyn, stage 2 back to Captain Rhodri; Lord Elidyn is a quest monster gamebots leave alone. An entry with "Replace": true replaces upstream's entry for its quest ID (otherwise upstream's wins): level 11 "Entry Into Tomorrow" (20157, 20155, 20156, 20159, 20158), rebuilt to the period story, is upstream's six stages with stage 2's marker on Frund at the red dwarf camp (deploy/bin/mob_fixes.json moves him there), stage 4 without upstream's lost-Crediac reissue by "Agisthil" (written for its old design), and Omis handing another Crediac at stage 6 to a player who lost it. "Chat": NPC replies to whispered keywords that replace upstream's, keyword by keyword (an empty reply silences one): the chain's dialogue, with deploy/bin/quest_dialogue.json; and the classic quests' period lines and names (quest entry scan 2026-10-11, with the world texts in quest_dialogue.json): the lines upstream's generator lost (Achae Smith, Sugnhild, Vadri Pade), Kaere's question as a key without the "?" OnWhisper trims, with the period's [get it for me], and the names it replaced with <Player> (Durren, Runil, Askheim, ...), which are keys too where upstream's key was <Player>; and (pass 2) the plain words it replaced with <Player> (Crace's "Aye, Well, it's", Keriann's "Yes, Yes"), the class said as a noun as <Class> (Skorri's "this fine Hunter", Thorgil's "a Spiritmaster like you"), Gral Bermorn's keys without the spaces upstream's kept, Nibalk's [Ibicus] (upstream's key was <Player>) and Kylirean's lines under his name (upstream's "Kyrilean" is no NPC's), with upstream's replies; and Wariel's and Amora's answer to the [name] their quests' texts ask again (quest_dialogue.json). Spec: docs/fork/specs/2026-10-09-epic-chains-design.md, section 3.2.

Captain Rhodri.matter: Sir Bors would have the support of the locals within Barfog, and this situation would be the best way to win their trust. Therefore your mission is to return to the renegade post and [dispatch] the outcasts.
Captain Rhodri.dispatch: You must ensure that justice is delivered to both Dillus and his [supporting] officers. When this is complete, visit the local outpost there and talk to one named Twr ap Alsig. We have it on good authority that if you win his support the locals will follow.
Captain Rhodri.down to business: We have trouble with the [Arawnites] along the border at Sauvage.
Captain Rhodri.Arawnites: They have gone quiet along the border at Sauvage, and quiet worries me more than noise. I need you to [speak with Lieutenant Kuebler] at Castle Sauvage.

Magus Agyfen.interested: Many in Camelot have begun to speak of your missions for Sir Bors. It seems you have succeeded where many others failed, and some of them resent it; I would watch my back around them. That is why I hesitate to give you this message from Captain Rhodri. I do not know what it says, only that I was told it would be very [profitable]. May whatever god you worship watch over you. Safe travels!

Twr ap Alsig.certain: The undead cythraul roam this land. Destroy one and bring me its skull, and Barfog will give you the support you seek.
Twr ap Alsig.goblin: Yes. They have a new order among them, and it is not their own. It is the result of an [outside influence].
Twr ap Alsig.outside influence: Dwarves, I am sure of it. There is a tunnel in Tepok's Mine, a [link to the borderlands], and through it they spread their foul word to the goblin hordes.
Twr ap Alsig.link to the borderlands: Find a Savant in the mine, one of their clever ones, and learn what you can of the passageways. You may be forced to slay the goblin and search his belongings.

Master Edric.interested: There is trouble in Snowdonia again. Captain Rhodri calls it routine, but Rhodri does not send for the Guild over routine. I have my [doubts].
Master Edric.doubts: I will say no more of it here. Will you go back to [Snowdonia]?

Master Arenis.interested: Rhodri's asking for us again. Says it's routine border trouble. If it were routine, he'd send his own men. I've got my [doubts].
Master Arenis.doubts: I will say no more of it here. Will you go back to [Snowdonia]?

Magus Isen.interested: Captain Rhodri writes of trouble in Snowdonia, which he calls routine. I have read a great many letters, and this one was written by a frightened man. I have my [doubts].
Magus Isen.doubts: I will say no more of it here. Will you go back to [Snowdonia]?

Yulia.interested: Captain Rhodri has sent for us again. He calls it routine, but the dead do not whisper of routine things. I have my [doubts].
Yulia.doubts: I will say no more of it here. Will you go back to [Snowdonia]?

Peze.interested: Rhodri's asking for us again. He calls it routine. Routine doesn't need a Reaver. I've got my [doubts].
Peze.doubts: I will say no more of it here. Will you go back to [Snowdonia]?

Hugh Gallen.bit of information: Listen close! Lord Prydwen once had a faithful cleric, known as Mulgrut. His service to our realm was unparallel. Yet, during Arthur's siege on Lancelot, his son, Durren, [was slain].

Achae Smith.out here: Oh, I know he meant well, thinking we could have a better life and all, that it would be less crowded than Camelot, which mind you, it is, but still... I guess I'm just sad is all. You see, my uncle, Thulin, went missing just a few days ago. I think one of Cabalist Meical's automotons got him, but I have no proof. Do you not know of [Cabalist Meical]?.
Achae Smith.another favor: Will you please find Thulin's remains for me? I would like to have a proper burial for him. It would mean so much to me if you [would fo this] for me.

Kaere.Will you gather the components for Keare: Enchanter Slone has called upon his knowledge of the magic of this land and combined it with my knowledge of the dead. Together the two make a powerful protection potion. All the components for the potion [can be found] on creatures that roam this land.
Kaere.get it for me: Enchanter Slone has called upon his knowledge of the magic of this land and combined it with my knowledge of the dead. Together the two make a powerful protection potion. All the components for the potion [can be found] on creatures that roam this land.

Vadri Pade.druid tale: Ah well I suppose to could be persuaded to speak it one last time. Have a seat and let us begin. Our story begins many generations ago. Our land was inhabited by a barbaric people and little if any order existed within Albion. Then fromt he northern shores came a strange mix calling themselves Celts. They spread through our land and suppressed the barbarians, absorbing the culture into their own. The priests of this new race were named [Druids] and they dominated in both religion and all daily deeds.

Sugnhild.loved one: Aye my friend, my husband was a wonderful man. His name was Fridgier and he was one of the most dashing men I have ever set eyes upon. He was sent on a mission by [Gudlor] and never returned. He said he could not tell me where he was going. I [searched many weeks] for him but to no avail.
Sugnhild.Gudlor: Gudlor is the town leader, Perhaps you should see him sometime.
Sugnhild.searched many weeks: While out one day, I was beset upon by this small sprite andhis followers. He laughed and called me names and then sapped me while I wasn't looking. When I awoke, I was in the bare and left in the woods to die. It was only by the hand of a Skadi that I was able to find furs and food enough to make it back to town. I have never gone out again for that creature stone the [ring] my husband gave me from my finger. All I have left to live for is my duty as a town guard.

Anrid.kept a piece: Svan's intention was that one-day, after the terrible unyielding winter that he and his sons would once again reunite and bring the Grenlock clan back together. Several says after Svan's sons left the northland, Svergird's Keep and its ancient stone walls were swept away by the white tide of ice and snow. The terrible storm took the old king with it, and all which remained of the northland. Svan's four sons, Coplin, Gunnar, Ove, and Div marched southward, tearing through [unknown territory].
Anrid.ready to continue: As you know Siv had three more brothers. The second brother Coplin decided since Siv was making new settlements outside of their new home that he would patrol the land. Coplin's goal was to protect all those who survived the journey from the northland. Coplin made friends with many of the creatures that lived in the surrounding areas. It was his goal to make pacts with these creatures so that the land would stay [safe] for all those that lived there, both human and creature.
Anrid.safe: Coplin was very successful in this attempt and many aggressions were worked through. Therefore many lived in peace during his lifetime. He lived a very long time, just as his brother Siv. His spirit resides on this plane in the forests of Myrkwood among his companions, the creatures of those forests. He may have information that will help you upon this journey. He can be found among the creatures of [Myrkwood].
Anrid.Myrkwood: Seek out Coplin's Spirit! Return to me when you have finished.

Danica.solve the mystery: Since Anrid came to me, I have been going through all the stories I know related to the Clan but I've reference to visitors from a far off land that resulted in the death of a girl of the clan named Freyana. Freyana was the most beloved daughter of the clan at the time these visitors came to Midgard. It was said she was so beautiful when she was born that she was named after the goddess of beauty, Freya. But [something happened] to her while she was still young.
Danica.His next entry: 'Ingvarr and his friends have been searching for a week now, but have not found the visitors. Everyone thought they had made it to their own lands until Runil showed up. He said that the deserters of the Clan had taken in the visitors and were making a deal with them. Runil feared the deal and left them, returning to the Clan. He begged to be accepted back into the Clan, but no one trusts him. The Alfevsons took him back in, but they secretly set someone to watch him at all times. I think Runil is [up to no good].'
Danica.up to no good: A few days later Ljagnid writes, 'I was right. Runil left us again today, but he said he wasn't returning to the deserters. He still feared the visitors. He told us he was going north, because he thought the visitors were going to do something bad to the Clan and to the deserters. Some people went with him, but we never saw any of them again. When he left, I saw him carrying a bunch of scrolls. I checked with everyone, but no one was missing any, so they must have belonged to Runil after all. Something strange is happening to me. I have started seeing strange creatures no one else sees. I am scared.' That is where the book ends. [Interesting], is it not?
Danica.angry: These members did not like the non-human races. They felt that co-existing with them rather than ruling them showed weakness. Rather than live in that situation, they packed up and left, following the loudest of them, Jango. I guess you could say they are the forerunners to the Blodfelags that roam the lands now. He led them out into the wilderness, where they roamed for a short time until they mysteriously died out. They had no name for themselves, but in the Clan they were referred to as the deserters. I also know of this man, [Runil].
Danica.Runil: I have a few notes about him in different books. He and his followers moved around quite a bit, but finally settled in Raumarik. It is said his spirit still haunts the land, although now he fears everyone, thinking they have been sent by either the deserters or the visitors. I believe the scrolls he took will contain the answer to what the visitors planned to do to the Clan. I need you to travel now to Raumarik and find Runil. His followers are always with him, hoping for his protection, so take many with you to defeat them. When you reach Raumarik, head to the river. Cross the river and head north until you find Runil. Return to me when you have the scrolls of Runil.

Nibalk.Ibicus: Yes, that large sea beast that's been devouring people everywhere. I understand that Ota, Karle, and Longbeard are all offering rewards for the carcass, to hang as trophies. I don't think that's what should be done! What a waste! No no no no listen to me. Take the carcass to the [Mussalkan].
Nibalk.Mussalkan: A creature like Ibicus is a gift to them! Althought they know him as Molvor. They can do so much with it! They will give you tokens, talismans, and trinkets of all sorts if you give them the carcass of a beast such as Ibicus! These trinkets and tokens, and the talismans, if you bring them to me, I will pay you not only for killing Ibicus, bu also for the trinkets they give you in exchange for the carcass! Think of it. It's worth more to ya!

Yver Tiu.sincere gratitude: Here you are friend. I had my compatriot, Averrius, look over the silk. He said it had properties that would benefit someone like you. I hope you can use it for some time to come. Again, I think you for all your hard work!
Yver Tiu.parts: My friend, Darrius, who lives in Fort Atla has recently made a strange discovery with some spinnerets. He wants me to look them over. Please take this note to him and bring the spinnerets back to me so I may further examine them.

Skorri.accuse one: Olvaerr here is one of Ota Yrling's Kobolds, who came over with Longbeard and his dwarves. He claims that Ailsa stole something of his. And Ailsa, one of Catla's followers claims that Olvaerr stole a totem she was taking to Catla Gardasdottir, I've been trying to reason with them but they both so stubborn that neither will listen to me when I say that perhaps they simply [lost their belongings].
Skorri.a cloak: Look Olvaerr, this fine <Class> has found your cloak! Please <Player>, give Olvaerr his cloak so that he will no longer think that Ailsa stole it from him. Perhaps he will even apologize to Alisa.

Kaisa.lost them: Yes, they lost them. A few days ago Ailsa went out with the totem tied to her belt and didn't come back with it. I'm sure she lost it when she was out studying the Morvaltar for Catla. As for Olvaerr, Ailsa might be right in hat he lost it in a drinking game [with the dwarves].
Kaisa.to meet Stonelock: Stonelock is going to be leading an expedition into the wilds of Gripklosa to track down the truth of yet another rumor about the Troll Fathers. I told Skorri to just go himself and leave both groups here and let Catla and Longbeard get in trouble for not being able to control their people, but Skorri said Stonelock wouldn't look at it that was. I'd hate for Skorri to [get in trouble] since he's been so kind to check on me while I've been sick.

Gazsi.nonsense: The sea beast, Ibicus. There are a few who have expressed interest in having the beast killed and returned to the town, to be displayed as a trophy! Rewards were promised, but still the Ibicus it is more valuable to the Musslaklan than it is to the leaders. It would also please me, more, to see the beast everyone around here is calling Ibicus give to the Musslaklan. They will use the remains to feed themselves, create items from the bones, and will find some uses for the [carcass], I imagine. They generally do.
Gazsi.carcass: Yes. Kill Ibicus, I agree. But don't take the carcass to those expeditionaries who want to display it on their walls or huts as trophies. They will pay you some money, but the musslaklan will pay you in tokens and trinkets. Turn the carcass of Ibicus in to a Musslaklan Trader and bring me the trinkets and tokens. The musslaklan know Ibicus as Movlor. Remember that. I will pay you a reward for the carcass, and I will pay you for the trinkets. It's your choice.

Edvard Averrson.far from the truth: The tomtes needed a place that wouldn't be taken over by the residents of the area. They searched and found a cave not far from where my brother watches them. They are crafty little men, and began to carve out a home for themselves under the earth. They worked quickly, and soon their new home was ready. Led by the strongest of the tomtes, Nisse, most of them left their lands and headed deep underground. Now, some people believe that the tomtes in the camps around here don't like dank surroundings of the cave, but that isn ot true. There is [another reason] they live above ground.
Edvard Averrson.another reason: All this time the tomtes have been planning ways to remove the inhabitants of Audliten and the surrounding areas and reclaim them for their own. The tomtes that live in the camps above ground are the eyes and ears for Nisse and report back everything they see. Recently I've noticed more messengers heading down from the north, yet my brother has not noticed and unusual activity around the entrance to the tomte caves. That has led us both to believe [someone else] is behind this plot to drive Thorgil and the others from this area off their land.
Edvard Averrson.eager to succeed: A long time ago, Smack displeased Nisse and was forced to leave the tomte caves and live among the races of Midgard. Since then, he has been working to get back into Nisse's good graces. It seems that he thinks if he can clear the land of invaders, as he sees them, then Nisse will be pleased and restore him to the position he once held. It appears that SMack has recruited Edigo to help in his plot. But now that Edigo is dead, Smack will try to recruit another of the tomtes. You must [stop Smack]!

Rollo.can't rest: Surely, the smith told you? My story is one [passed down] the line of dwarven smiths. The story of how I, Rollo, failed my master, Brack.
Rollo.passed down: Aye, it is passed down. Brack left me to care for items he had forged or helped create for use by all Dwarves. I failed! Ugnof and his men heard of this changeable item and [stole it].
Rollo.stole it: Aye, stole it. Killed me. For 300 years, the spawn of Ugnof have been carrying the Brack item. For 300 years I have wandered these hills cursing his name! I shall not rest until someone can [retrieve the Brack item].
Rollo.retrieve the Brack item: Aye, fare well, then, seek out Ugnof Toestubber in the lands named Western Svealand (You will find Ugnof walking outside the perimeter of Hugginfel with a Blodfeleg [Thralldriver] and a Blodfeleg Warhound, both will join in the fight.) Return with Brack to Hilde, in Haggerfel, and my soul shall rest!

Sentry Dwarn.tale: Wonderful, let me tell you of [Morana], the pious Saracen.
Sentry Dwarn.Morana: Aye, Morana, never a more pious woman was to be had here in Midgard. She was a slave here, brought back from a raid on a settlement in northern Albion. She never complained about her plight, but she continuously [prayed].

Atzar.had his belongings: There was a disagreement between the rwo werewolves, and the one left, taking some of the others with him. They came here to Myrkwood and settled into the forest, not far from here. At first, the residents if the town, Askheim, did not know of their presence. Understand that back then, the werewolves had a human form during the day. It has only been over time that they changed and assumed the form the have today. I do not know the entire story, but I know that something bad happened and it resulted in the werewolves taking over [Askheim].
Atzar.to recover: I'm sure Curka talked about the svartlafs when you were with her. She always talks about them and how bad they get treated. Well, I can see why they get treated that way after what they did to me! While you were away, I wanted to get a peek at what the werewolves were up to. Living so close to Askheim, it's natural to want to know what's going on. While I was out in the forest I got attacked by the svartalfs! They seemed to think I [support the werewolves].
Atzar.Askheim: The werewolves that live there now raise their young and let them tear up the land and terrorize the people. It was those pups that attacked me and stole Trustan's favorite sword. I know Trustan would want it back, and I'd go and get it from him, but have some other things of his to find. Trustan loaned a few of this things to another friend and I must get those things back before I can send everything up to him. Please, seek out the werewolf pups that scamper behind Gna Faste and get back Trustan's sword. Please!

Arnleif.Krrrck: Ah such a sad tale. Originally, Krrrck was a priest of Skadi, helping oyung Hunters learn the ways of the woods, as well as tutoring villagers on how to survive the harsh winters. His name was [Erik].
Arnleif.Erik: Erik was very improtant to Skadi, and she rewarded him well for his services. Loki, ever the mischief-maker, decided to trick Skadi and turned her friendly priest into a [frog].
Arnleif.frog: A large troll indeed! When the Goddess came to find Erik, all she found in his temple was this large frog. Not knowing what had happened to Erik, Skadi went in [search] of him.
Arnleif.miserable: Skadi, still unhappy with the disappearance of her priest, took the frog to [Skona Ravine] where he could be with other wildlife.
Arnleif.Skona Ravine: Skona Ravine and a wonderous place, filled with many creatures and various healing plants. It is said that Erik wishes to be released from his [imprisonment] and rejoined with his goddess, Skadi.

Crace.enchanted silver: Aye, Well, it's mainly controlled by those evil siabra local to the area, however, I've a friend who has managed to get a large amount of the silver. See, we've come up with a trade. The next boat leaves for Hibernia shortly, and I don't have the time to go and get everything to trade myself. See, there are many things here that may be valuable back in the mainland. I've arranged a trade. All I need right now, though, is two sporites.

Keriann.hamlet: Oh! Another one wanting to know about the Path of Harmony, eh? Well, I'm not a Mentalist, but I've studied their ways. Mentalists draw strength from understanding that everything works together, that the magical world and the non-magical world are really the same world. There is a balance between magic and non-magic. It's only when both are used together that there is harmony. Now, go speak with Cadalind, at the guard tower, to learn of the Path of Focus. Yes, Yes, I know you already spoke with her, but I've not studied the path Eldritches follow.

Thorgil.staff: You cannot use a bow, <Player>. Perhaps a <Class> like you would prefer a nice [staff]?

Gral Bermorn.switch: As the last rays of light fade from Salisbury, travel to each major druid ring and make use of your crystal. The crystal will be crushed in the process and will activate the ring's well. As Morgana's power has hold of the tombs below these rings, I am unsure what the mix of necromantic power and ley energy will have upon you and the circle itself. Be prepared for anything! If you find yourself without a ley crystal return to a minor circle and use the darkenstone to gain another. If you are foolish enough to lose your darkenstone, you may return to the [ axis circle ] and kill a skeleton to obtain another.
Gral Bermorn.axis circle: All seven of the wells can only be activated using darkness. If dawn arrives and you have not visited all seven you must wait till the next night to complete the ritual. When you have established the alignment of these ley lines, travel to the heart of Stonehenge and use your darkenstone for the final time. Upon the stone's destruction the bonds that tie the portal close should ignite and allow it to be [ opened from the other side ].
Gral Bermorn.opened from the other side: You must be ready for Glasan at this point. When the arch druid arrives, you will have little time to attack him, as his power will grow quickly. If you are successful in slaying him, the staff should shatter on its own. Any shards left from the battle must be returned to me! Here, take these instructions to aid you. Good luck to thee Theurgist.

Kylirean.experiment: Aye, I think I have discovered a way to make comfortable and stylish armour, but I'm afraid people around here would look [down] on me if they knew what I needed to make it.
Kylirean.down: You see those lough wolf cadgers? Their pelts make for excellent armor, if you can believe it. With this new tanning process I have been working on, it is lighter, more durable, and softer than any other [hide] I have ever worked with.
Kylirean.hide: Therein lies my problem, <Player>. You see, there are folks here in Mag Mell that are trying to save the little beasts, if you can believe that. If they saw me kill one, they would go absolutely insane with fury. That's why I need you to [help me out].
Kylirean.help me out: I'd like for you to get me a lough wolf cadger pelt. You are anonymous enough that no one will care. Do you think you can do that for me?
Kylirean.item: What I need now is a rock chert from a mudman. I can use the chert to smooth out the pelt and make the leather supple. Find a mudman and get the chert for me.

Wariel.name: Well, it is a pleasure to meet you. I enjoy meeting all the young Vikings throughoout our [realm].

Amora.name: It is a pleasure to meet you. I am so glad you have come to aid me and [Magnild].
